Bitcoin & Infrastructure

A Thousand Mines Hijacked in One Second as Unencrypted Plumbing Fails Around a Sound Chain

Braiins traces a three-week BGP hijacking campaign over unencrypted Stratum V1 that diverted up to 1.9 EH/s across more than a thousand European sites in a single second, as wallet rebroadcast leaks and bogus Electrum servers expose the unauthenticated plumbing around Bitcoin.

At 09:31 UTC on November 20, between 1,050 and 1,600 European mining sites dropped their pool connections in the same second, reconnected to the same hostname and IP address, and kept hashing at full speed while their own dashboards read zero [s536]. Forensic findings published by Braiins on November 25 and dissected across Nostr today show neither the ASICs nor the pools were breached: attackers announced narrower BGP prefixes to intercept plaintext Stratum V1 traffic, masqueraded as the pool, and forwarded the stolen shares under their own account [s536] [s531].

Across three weeks — nineteen episodes in Latin America, one packet capture in Brazil, and four European waves inside a single hour — the campaign peaked at 1.9 exahashes per second yet probably cleared less than $17,000, roughly a twelfth of a single block reward [s536]. Eleven years ago, Dell SecureWorks documented the same trick netting $83,000; today, thinner hashprice has shrunk the haul even as the technique spreads to address blocks hosting most major pools [s536] [s520].

Dr -ck noted that clustered industrial farms are the easiest targets, whereas the roughly 50,000 small, distributed miners on solo ckpool are harder to corral [s26]. Both Dr -ck and 21 Milioni di Chiacchiere urged operators to abandon stratum+tcp:// — including backup endpoints — for authenticated Stratum V2, a local proxy such as ckproxy, or OCEAN’s DATUM gateway [s26] [s531]. As Braiins put it in the report cited by Roger, with encryption in place, The attacker does not earn any bitcoin. [s536]

The mining alert landed beside two quieter reminders that the chain verifies while its surrounding plumbing often does not. A Delving Bitcoin disclosure showed that an unconfirmed 309-satoshi transaction (about 18 cents) can exploit Bitcoin Core’s 12-to-36-hour wallet rebroadcast timer to link addresses to node IPs — succeeding 30 times out of 30 in regtest, including against watch-only wallets [s536]. Meanwhile, fake Electrum servers flagged by 0xB10C were confirmed to be feeding crafted transactions aimed at unpatched servers [s520].

Protocol, Security & The Open Stack

Nostr Protocol

NIP 5E Aims to Shrink a Million Reactions to a Few Kilobytes

hodlbod opened pull request 2557 on the Nostr NIPs repository proposing NIP 5E, a protocol for arbitrary event aggregations that clients can merge across relays and audit for forgeries [s196]. A million kind 7 events is about 500 MB. NIP 5E drops that to a few KB. [s196]

The same day, hodlbod shipped Flotilla 1.6.0 with improved network feeds, threaded dialogs, and background Android audio [s275], plus Dipity, a Nostr community board that trades posts with nearby phones over Bluetooth. Elsewhere on the open web, hzrd149 gave nsite.lol a fresh design [s147], and oliver released Mirall (mirall.app), an open-source P2P file-transfer tool with no size limit or third-party relay lock-in [s122] [s236].

Private Provider Routes Around Zapstore; Linux Amethyst Flagged for Audit

Private Provider shipped version 0.7.12 — updating bundled ngit, Node, Pi, and routstrd — and announced it is leaving Zapstore after its companion non-APK archive left releases stuck pending [s510]. Updates now move straight from Blossom to Obtainium via a single-tap nsite page [s510].

Sovereignty & The State

FinCEN Offline, Swiss CARF Set for 2028, and a 20-Year US Lock

Coincards.com noted that FinCEN — the US Treasury bureau that collects suspicious activity reports — took systems offline after confirming unauthorized access [s103], while Britain signed an EU digital-wallet cooperation deal just months after scrapping its domestic digital ID card [s55].

In Europe, 21 Milioni di Chiacchiere reported that Switzerland’s Federal Council approved 57 jurisdictions, including all 27 EU states and the UK, for automatic crypto tax reporting under CARF beginning in 2028 — warning that centralized KYC databases have repeatedly fed physical wrench attacks across Europe [s530]. In Washington, H.R. 8957, which would codify a 20-year no-sell lock on seized federal bitcoin, reached the House Union Calendar ahead of the 119th Congress’s January 3 expiration [s536].

Machines, Proofs & The Quantum Sanity Check

Artificial Intelligence

When AI Proves Riemann — and Leaves Humans Asking Why

[bit] max⚡️ examined the aftermath of mathematician Levent Alpöge and Claude producing a formal Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis — originally some 17 million lines of code — verified by the Lean and Mathlib community [s512]. Formal checkers can certify logical validity, [bit] max⚡️ wrote, yet Michael Rubinstein’s human-readable exposition remains unfinished, raising a sharper question for science and software alike: what happens when machines hand us verified answers faster than we can understand the path that produced them [s512]?

That tension echoed across the feed. Sebastix highlighted a passage from dergigi’s essay Taste and Values marvelling that development now feels effortless [s503], while Christoph Ono built a side experiment in two hours using 15 prompts running in the background [s17]. Yet Roger’s look at Wallet of Satoshi’s new “Connect your AI” feature praised its restraint: agents can read balances and request payments, but face a 300-second human approval veto and a three-request cap — The agent never holds anything that can spend. [s538] Meanwhile, the EFF welcomed Signal’s move to block AI agents [s215], and redshift detailed using the Tinfoil SDK inside Routstr so E2EE inference stays encrypted straight to source providers [s53].

On the balance-sheet side, LL62 surfaced a TFTC analysis comparing AI’s infrastructure buildout to the 1990s telecom bust: Anthropic generated approximately $4.59 billion in revenue in 2025 while committing more than $895 billion in future infrastructure spend. That is over $100 pledged for every $1 earned last year. [s506] [s507] [s509] And a RAND brief cited by Roger warned that AI displacing 10 to 15 percent of high-earning work hours threatens a federal tax base that now draws 84 percent of its revenue from individual income and payroll taxes [s536].

Cryptography

No Real Shor Factoring in 2026, Says waxwing

Cutting through post-quantum panic, waxwing posted a brisk tally of actual 2026 quantum hardware milestones: Nothing in 2026 counts as Shor on real hardware doing something real. [s169] The honest high-water marks remain 15 (from 2001) and a heavily compiled 21 (from 2012). Project Eleven’s April 1 BTC prize for breaking a 15-bit elliptic-curve key on IBM hardware was reproduced by Jonas Schnelli in 20 lines of Python using random bits and by Yuval Adam using /dev/urandom [s169].

On the stricter benchmark that matters — error-corrected logical qubits with no runs thrown out — waxwing noted the highest count as of October 2026 is 8, at Quantinuum, with high error rates [s183]. Still, Blockstream’s research director warned at a New York workshop cited by markusturm that post-quantum migration is a coordination problem that takes years regardless of the hardware calendar [s520].

TanukiBTC ⚡ supplied the day’s comic relief, deadpanning that three prompts into Claude had bypassed Razborov-Rudich with a Mind-Goblin oracle: Cryptography is officially over. Withdraw your Bitcoin before Monday. [s29]
